newsitem.title: GREECE: BASKETBALL-OLYMPIAKOS' GRAY TESTS POSITIVE FOR EPHEDRINE.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-OLYMPIAKOS' GRAY TESTS POSITIVE FOR EPHEDRINE.

text.p: Olympiakos' American guard Evric Gray has tested positive for the banned substance ephedrine and will probably miss Europe's Final Four basketball championship next week, club officials said on Wednesday.

"His first sample was positive. The situation is difficult because if he tests positive in the second sample, which is the most probable case, he will be punished," Olympiakos' Serb coach Dusan Ivkovic told reporters.
Gray usually plays as a substitute for team captain George Sigalas. If he tests positive a second time he faces a three-month ban by FIBA, the international federation.
"It is not such a big loss but the coach must work around it as Sigalas is our main defender and fouls a lot," another club official said.
Gray, who signed for Olympiakos this season, was tested by FIBA officials this month before a EuroLeague quarter-final clash with fellow Greek club Panathiniakos.

"He was getting a vitamin called 'Up the Gas' which is sold over the counter in the United States but not in Europe. I believe him that he was using it without knowing it contained banned substances," Ivkovic said.
Olympiakos, finalists in 1994 and 1995, are considered the favourites along with Spain's Barcelona for this year's crown. The championship is in Rome from April 22-24.
